newsitem.title: USA: US corp bond mart absorbs new globals, awaits more.
newsitem.headline: US corp bond mart absorbs new globals, awaits more.

text.p: Global debt offerings are expected to be the focus of the day once more as Wednesday's positive reception to several deals triggers other players to tap the U.S. corporate bond market, dealers said.
"Yesterday's global deals went very well," said one player. "Because of the positive reaction other players are tapping the market."
On Thursday, joint lead managers Hongkong Shanghai Bank and JP Morgan Securities launched a US$1.0 billion global five-year debt offering for the United Mexican States, players said.
The deal is expected to price at LIBOR plus 140 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, players said.
Looking ahead, Poland is expected to tap the market with a $500 million yankee issue via JP Morgan Securities, they said.

Wednesday's global supply included a $1.0 billion 10-year AAA-rated bond issue from Bayerische Landesbank's New York branch, priced via Merrill Lynch & Co Inc and J.P. Morgan to yield 25 basis points over Treasuries.
Also, American Express Co sold $500 million in A1/A-plus rated seven-year global debt, priced to yield 39 basis points off the curve via Lehman Brothers.
The Republic of South Africa also brought its much-awaited $500 million 20-year Baa3/BB-plus rated Yankee issues which priced to yield 183 basis points over Treasuries, players said.

Among other investment grade issues priced on Wednesday were Salomon Inc's $400 million three-year deal which priced at 58 basis points over; and Toro Corp's $175 million of Baa3/BBB-minus rated two-tranche debt to yield 80 basis points over for 10-year paper and 113 basis points over for 30-years.
Dealers said Salomon's issue tightened two-to-four basis when freed to trade in the secondary market.
On Thursday, Connecticut Light & Power is slated to bring $200 million in five-year first mortgage bonds, players said.

In addition, a few names remain on the new issue calendar including an RJR Nabisco $350 million two-part debt offering, via joint managers Morgan Stanley & Co Inc and Merrill Lynch & Co, syndicate sources said.
The RJR deal is expected to include a $150 million seven-year issue as well as a $200 million 10-year issue.
In addition, Pohang Iron & Steel is expected to bring $300 million in 10-year debt via JP Morgan Securities Inc, players said.
Turning to the high-yield sector, several issues are slated to come to market by the end of this week, players said.
Equimar Shipholdings Ltd's will sell $100 million in 144A 10-year notes via Credit Suisse First Boston. Price talk on the issue is seen between 9.625 - 9.875 percent, sources said.

Oxford Automotive Inc is slated to bring a $125 million offering of 10-year 144A senior subordinated notes via Salomon Brothers, sources said. Price talk is seen between 375 basis points and 400 basis points over Treasuries, they said.

Also, Echostar DBS Corp will sell $325 million in five-year senior secured notes via Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette Securities, players said. Price talk on the issue is seen between 12.25 - 12.50 percent.
Boyd Gaming Corp is expected to issue $250 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes via Salomon Brothers, sources said.
Leiner Health Products Group is also slated to bring a $85 million 144A 10-year debt deal via Merrill Lynch & Co. Spread talk is seen in the area of 9.75 percent, sources said.

On Wednesday, Horseshoe Gaming LLC's sold $165 million in 10-year B3/single-B rated senior subordinated notes, priced as 9-3/8s to yield 300 basis points over Treasuries via Wasserstein Perella (Grantchester Securities,) according to a high-yield trading source.
Also, late Wednesday, Coach USA sold $150 million in 10-year 144A notes to yield 9.375 percent, or 296 basis points over Treasuries, sources said.
Meanwhile, players said deals priced recently in the junk sector have traded off with the broadcasting credits taking the brunt of the pressure.
Young Broadcasting's recent 10-year senior subordinated note deal was quoted at 98-1/2 bid on Thursday compared with an original level of 99.08. In late trade yesterday, the issue was quoted 98 bid.
Jacor Communications' $150 million 10-year senior subordinated notes, priced last week at par, were quoted off 1/4 point on Thursday, players said.

One exception was Chancellor Broadcasting's $200 million 10-year senior subordinated notes, said one player. The notes were trading at a 99-3/4 bid in the secondary market compared with Wednesday's issued level of 98.887.
Separately, in the government market, the benchmark U.S. Treasury bond was off 10/32 at 98-28/32 to yield 6.71 percent.
(( -- Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675 ))
